## SPFxApplicationCustomizerProvider

Establishes SPFx context and isolated runtime state for an Application Customizer React surface. Pass its initialized native instance. Descendants mount after the active ServiceScope finishes; the provider never registers, finishes or authorizes services. The missing-scope fallback allows rendering but service-consuming hooks can fail.

Host renders reconcile shallow property snapshots, including removals and reference changes; nested in-place changes are not deep-observed. Hook property updates synchronize back to the native instance. Theme subscriptions and runtime listeners are cleaned up on unmount; obsolete scope-readiness callbacks are ignored. Keep a mounted provider associated with its owning host surface and unmount React when that surface is disposed.

### Imports

```ts
import { SPFxApplicationCustomizerProvider } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { SPFxApplicationCustomizerProvider } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/core';
```

### Use when

- toolkit hooks render inside a native ApplicationCustomizer surface owned by this host instance.

### Avoid when

- the host is another SPFx component kind; use its matching typed provider.

### Examples

#### Mount an initialized native host

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { BaseApplicationCustomizer } from '@microsoft/sp-application-base';
import { SPFxApplicationCustomizerProvider, SPFxApplicationCustomizerProviderProps } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

function hostTree(instance: BaseApplicationCustomizer<{ title: string }>): React.ReactElement {
  const props: SPFxApplicationCustomizerProviderProps<{ title: string }> = { instance, children: <span>Host content</span> };
  return <SPFxApplicationCustomizerProvider {...props} />;
}
```

#### Retry late placeholders and dispose captured roots

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import * as ReactDom from 'react-dom';
import { BaseApplicationCustomizer, PlaceholderContent, PlaceholderName } from '@microsoft/sp-application-base';
import { SPFxApplicationCustomizerProvider, useSPFxProperties } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

interface IMyCustomizerProps {
  headerMessage: string;
}

const HeaderComponent: React.FC = () => {
  const { properties } = useSPFxProperties<IMyCustomizerProps>();
  return <header>{properties?.headerMessage ?? 'Welcome'}</header>;
};

export default class MyApplicationCustomizer extends BaseApplicationCustomizer<IMyCustomizerProps> {
  private topPlaceholder?: PlaceholderContent;

  public onInit(): Promise<void> {
    this.context.placeholderProvider.changedEvent.add(this, this.renderTopPlaceholder);
    this.renderTopPlaceholder();
    return Promise.resolve();
  }

  public onDispose(): void {
    this.context.placeholderProvider.changedEvent.remove(this, this.renderTopPlaceholder);
    const placeholder = this.topPlaceholder;
    this.topPlaceholder = undefined;
    if (placeholder) {
      ReactDom.unmountComponentAtNode(placeholder.domElement);
      placeholder.dispose();
    }
  }

  private renderTopPlaceholder = (): void => {
    if (!this.topPlaceholder) {
      const capturedPlaceholder = this.context.placeholderProvider.tryCreateContent(
        PlaceholderName.Top,
        {
          onDispose: () => {
            if (capturedPlaceholder) {
              ReactDom.unmountComponentAtNode(capturedPlaceholder.domElement);
              if (this.topPlaceholder === capturedPlaceholder) {
                this.topPlaceholder = undefined;
              }
            }
          }
        }
      );
      this.topPlaceholder = capturedPlaceholder;
    }

    if (!this.topPlaceholder) return;
    const element = React.createElement(
      SPFxApplicationCustomizerProvider,
      { instance: this },
      React.createElement(HeaderComponent)
    );
    ReactDom.render(element, this.topPlaceholder.domElement);
  };
}
```

#### Render and dispose each field cell

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import * as ReactDom from 'react-dom';
import {
  BaseFieldCustomizer,
  IFieldCustomizerCellEventParameters
} from '@microsoft/sp-listview-extensibility';
import { SPFxFieldCustomizerProvider } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

function FieldRenderer({ value }: { value: unknown }) { return <span>{String(value ?? '')}</span>; }

interface IMyFieldProps {
  colorMapping: Record<string, string>;
}

export default class MyFieldCustomizer extends BaseFieldCustomizer<IMyFieldProps> {
  public onRenderCell(event: IFieldCustomizerCellEventParameters): void {
    const element = React.createElement(
      SPFxFieldCustomizerProvider,
      { instance: this },
      React.createElement(FieldRenderer, {
        value: event.fieldValue
      })
    );
    ReactDom.render(element, event.domElement);
  }

  public onDisposeCell(event: IFieldCustomizerCellEventParameters): void {
    ReactDom.unmountComponentAtNode(event.domElement);
    super.onDisposeCell(event);
  }
}
```

Descendants mount after the active ServiceScope finishes; the provider never registers, finishes or authorizes services. The missing-scope fallback allows rendering but service-consuming hooks can fail.

#### Dispose a temporary command dialog root

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import * as ReactDom from 'react-dom';
import { BaseListViewCommandSet, type IListViewCommandSetExecuteEventParameters } from '@microsoft/sp-listview-extensibility';
import { SPFxListViewCommandSetProvider } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
function DetailsDialog({ count, onClose }: { count: number; onClose: () => void }) {
  return <section role="dialog" aria-label="Selected rows"><p>{count} selected</p><button onClick={onClose}>Close</button></section>;
}
export default class DetailsCommand extends BaseListViewCommandSet<{ dialogTitle: string }> {
  private closeDialog?: () => void;
  public onExecute(event: IListViewCommandSetExecuteEventParameters): void {
    if (event.itemId !== 'SHOW_DETAILS') return;
    this.closeDialog?.();
    const root = document.createElement('div');
    document.body.appendChild(root);
    const close = () => {
      ReactDom.unmountComponentAtNode(root);
      root.remove();
      if (this.closeDialog === close) this.closeDialog = undefined;
    };
    this.closeDialog = close;
    ReactDom.render(<SPFxListViewCommandSetProvider instance={this}>
      <DetailsDialog count={this.context.listView.selectedRows?.length ?? 0} onClose={close} />
    </SPFxListViewCommandSetProvider>, root);
  }
  public onDispose(): void { this.closeDialog?.(); }
}
```

## SPFxWebPartProvider

Establishes SPFx context and isolated runtime state for a WebPart React surface. Pass its initialized native instance. Descendants mount after the active ServiceScope finishes; the provider never registers, finishes or authorizes services. The missing-scope fallback allows rendering but service-consuming hooks can fail.

Host renders reconcile shallow property snapshots, including removals and reference changes; nested in-place changes are not deep-observed. Hook property updates synchronize back to the native instance. Theme subscriptions and runtime listeners are cleaned up on unmount; obsolete scope-readiness callbacks are ignored. Keep a mounted provider associated with its owning host surface and unmount React when that surface is disposed.

### Imports (7)

```ts
import { SPFxWebPartProvider } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { SPFxWebPartProvider } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/core';
```

### Use when (4)

- toolkit hooks render inside a native WebPart surface owned by this host instance.

### Avoid when (4)

- the host is another SPFx component kind; use its matching typed provider.

WebPart providers expose the native domElement and current display mode. Container hooks perform observation when mounted; the provider itself does not observe the element. Other current providers publish no container element or display mode. Provider isolation covers local runtime state, while explicitly shared clients, tenant data and caller objects retain their own sharing contracts.

### Examples (7)

#### Mount an initialized native host (4)

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { BaseClientSideWebPart } from '@microsoft/sp-webpart-base';
import { SPFxWebPartProvider, SPFxWebPartProviderProps } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';

function hostTree(instance: BaseClientSideWebPart<{ title: string }>): React.ReactElement {
  const props: SPFxWebPartProviderProps<{ title: string }> = { instance, children: <span>Host content</span> };
  return <SPFxWebPartProvider {...props} />;
}
```

#### WebPart render and disposal

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import * as ReactDom from 'react-dom';
import { BaseClientSideWebPart } from '@microsoft/sp-webpart-base';
import { SPFxWebPartProvider, useSPFxProperties } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
interface Properties { title: string; }
function Title() {
  const { properties } = useSPFxProperties<Properties>();
  return <h2>{properties?.title ?? 'Loading'}</h2>;
}
export default class TitleWebPart extends BaseClientSideWebPart<Properties> {
  public render(): void {
    ReactDom.render(<SPFxWebPartProvider instance={this}><Title /></SPFxWebPartProvider>, this.domElement);
  }
  protected onDispose(): void { ReactDom.unmountComponentAtNode(this.domElement); }
}
```

    );

}
